predictions.source_summary: The remoteUrl variable originates from tmpPath, which is returned by createCustomRemote function. The createCustomRemote function uses startCommand and endCommand parameters that are passed into the main function. These commands are executed via utils.run() in the createCustomRemote function, but their values are not validated or sanitized before being used to construct a git clone command.
predictions.sink_summary: The git clone command is executed with shell interpolation, where remoteUrl (which can be an arbitrary path) is directly interpolated into the command string without any sanitization or validation.
predictions.guard_summary: There are no validation, sanitization, or parameterization controls in place to prevent malicious input from being used in the git clone command. The commands passed to createCustomRemote are executed as-is without any checks on their contents.
predictions.risk_pattern: Command injection vulnerability where user-provided or attacker-controlled command strings can be executed through shell interpolation in a git clone operation
predictions.context_summary: The code path is triggered when createCustomDiff is true. In this case, the function calls createCustomRemote which executes startCommand and endCommand in a temporary directory. The return value of createCustomRemote (a temporary directory path) becomes remoteUrl, which is then used in a git clone command with shell interpolation.
